newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Continental Airlines is in negotiations to buy its planes exclusively from Boeing, according to Continental's top executive.
* The Dow Jones industrials wiped out the rest of this year's gains, finishing down 148.36 points on Friday at 6,391.69.
* March producer prices, excluding food and energy, rose 0.4 percent.
* Singapore's Neptune Orient announced plans to buy container carrier APL for $825 million.
* Patriot American is set to announce plans to buy Wyndham Hotel and some hotels controlled by the Trammel Crow family for around $1 billion.
* Time Warner is taking its New Line Cinema off the market and is near to securing bank financing for the movie company's production slate.
* Uncertainty faces Travelers' plans to issue stock options to employee 401(k) plans.
* Among the 25 worst performers in Friday's stock market decline were several large-company stock funds.
* Tyco International said it would buy AT&T's undersea cable operation for $850 million.
* Odyssey Partners plans to sell William Scottsman to two companies for $675 million in cash and assumed debt, according to people close to the matter.
* Todd Stitzer was named president and chief executive of Cadbury Schweppes' Dr. Pepper/Seven Up unit.
* Dean Witter's top officer was paid $4.3 million in cash and stock last year.
* Meditrust SBI agreed to buy Santa Anita Cos in a reverse-merger valued at $383 million in stock.
* Heard on the Street: Trouble may be brewing on Capitol Hill for Raytheon and other defense contractors in the throes of industry consolidation.
* Credit markets: With inflation threatening to rear its ugly head as the economy sizzles, investors might start paying more attention to those inflation-indexed bonds.
